segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, holy brothers and sisters, sharers in a heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who was faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses also was in his house.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For he has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, to the same degree that the builder of a house has greater honor than the house.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For every house is built by someone, but the one who built everything is God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Moses was faithful in all his house as a servant, as a witness to the things that would be spoken later,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but Christ was faithful as a son over his house. We are his house, if we hold fast our confidence and the hope in which we boast.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Today, if you hear his voice,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, as on the day of testing in the wilderness,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: where your ancestors tested me, putting me to the proof, and saw my works

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: for forty years. That is why I was disgusted with this generation and said, ‘They always go astray in their hearts, and they have not known my ways.’

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: So I swore in my anger, ‘They shall never enter my rest.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: See to it, brothers and sisters, that none of you has an evil heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you is hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For we have become sharers in Christ, if indeed we hold fast our first resolve, firm to the end.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As it is said:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For who were they who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt led by Moses?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And with whom was he disgusted for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose corpses fell in the wilderness?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not to those who disobeyed?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.

notes.note: This is the only place in the New Testament where Jesus is called an apostle. The word means someone sent with a commission, an envoy. Here it presents Jesus as the one sent by God, paired with his role as high priest representing the people to God.

The Greek verb is the ordinary word for 'make' and could be read as 'the one who made him'. Most translators take it as 'appointed', a sense it has in the Septuagint (for example of God 'making' Moses and Aaron in 1 Samuel 12:6), and that fits the context of office and faithfulness.

The wording echoes Numbers 12:7, where God says of Moses, 'he is faithful in all my house'. 'His house' is therefore God's house, meaning God's household or people, not Moses' own. The argument that follows plays on 'house' as both a building and a household.

The Greek word, used only here in the New Testament, is taken from the Septuagint of Numbers 12:7. It is not the common word for a slave but a more dignified term for a personal attendant who serves freely. The contrast with Christ is therefore between an honoured attendant in the household and the son set over it.

notes.phrase: the hope in which we boast
notes.traditional: the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end
notes.note: Many manuscripts add 'firm to the end' after these words, and older English versions include it. The phrase is absent from some of the earliest witnesses and was probably copied in from verse 14, where it is original. SBLGNT omits it.

The quotation in verses 7–11 is Psalm 95:7–11 in its Greek form. Where the Hebrew psalm names the places Meribah and Massah (Exodus 17:1–7), the Greek version translates the names as 'rebellion' and 'testing'. The related verb in verse 16 is rendered 'rebelled' to keep the link.

In the psalm itself the forty years belong with what follows: God was displeased with that generation for forty years. The wording here, with 'that is why' inserted after the phrase, attaches the forty years to seeing God's works. The author knows the other division too and uses it in verse 17.

notes.traditional: I was angry with / I was grieved with / I was provoked with
notes.note: Most translations have 'angry' or 'provoked'. In the Septuagint, which is nearly the only place the verb is found, it regularly translates Hebrew words for loathing or being repelled by something. 'Disgusted' reflects that usage and keeps the verb distinct from the ordinary word for anger in verse 11.

notes.phrase: They shall never enter my rest
notes.traditional: They shall not enter into my rest
notes.note: The Greek reads literally 'if they shall enter my rest', a Hebrew oath formula with the penalty clause left unspoken ('may such-and-such happen to me if...'). It amounts to an emphatic denial. In the psalm the 'rest' is the promised land, which the exodus generation was barred from entering (Numbers 14:20–35); the next chapter develops a larger meaning.

The Greek word is the negative of the word translated 'faithful' in verses 2 and 5, and can mean either lack of trust or lack of faithfulness. 'Unbelief' follows the Numbers 14 background, where the people refuse to trust God's promise. The sense of disloyalty is also in view, as 'turns away' and the 'disobeyed' of verse 18 show.

The phrase can mean those who share in Christ, participating in him and what he gives, or those who share with Christ, his partners or companions. The same word clearly means 'companions' in 1:9, but takes the sense 'sharers in' at 3:1 and 6:4. Translations and commentators are divided.

notes.traditional: our original confidence / the beginning of our confidence
notes.note: Most translations render this 'confidence' or 'assurance'. Lexicographers have questioned whether the word has that subjective sense in this period. Its attested meanings include 'underlying reality' (as in 1:3) and, in Hellenistic historians, a firm stand or steadfast resolve. The latter fits the call to hold firm here. Others take it as 'the reality we began with', and 'confidence' remains the majority rendering.

notes.phrase: who were they who heard and yet rebelled
notes.traditional: For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses
notes.note: The earliest manuscripts had no accents, and the first word can be read as 'who?' or as 'some'. The King James Version took it as 'some' and made the verse a statement. Nearly all modern editors and translators read a question, matching the two parallel questions in verses 17 and 18.

candidates.reason: Occurs in Hebrews 1:3, 3:14, 11:1 and 2 Corinthians 9:4, 11:17, where the traditional 'confidence/assurance' is lexically disputed and translations diverge widely, so the senses need one coordinated decision.
The plural address to mixed congregations recurs throughout the letters and Acts, and 'brothers' versus 'brothers and sisters' must be settled once.
Recurs across John, Acts, Paul and Hebrews with renderings varying between 'boldness', 'confidence', 'openness' and 'plainly'; the senses need to be mapped consistently.
Very frequent, and translators vary between 'encourage', 'exhort', 'urge', 'comfort' and 'appeal'; readers would benefit from a fixed rendering per sense.
The negative of the register word πίστις can mean 'unbelief' or 'unfaithfulness' (Romans 3:3), and should be coordinated with the faith/faithfulness decision.
